plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down. Bidding exactly my value of $5 ensures I only win when profitable (value exceeds the price I'd pay) and maximizes expected profit. I'll bid my true value.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding exactly my value of $48 ensures I win whenever profitable (when my value exceeds others' bids) and never overpay, while not sacrificing potential profit by bidding lower. There's no incentive to shade my bid in this format.

In a second-price auction, bidding truthfully (bidding exactly my value) is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. This is because I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid, so there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down. Bidding my true value of $27 maximizes my expected profit whether I win or lose, since overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, and underbidding risks losing profitable auctions.
